summary:
We developed an interactive, browser-based 3D lunar mission simulation built with Three.js, TypeScript, and custom low-poly PBR assets generated procedurally in Blender. Spanning multiple mission stages—from an orbital EVA Ready Room and launch sequence to a Lunar South Pole outpost—players suit up in rigged Artemis xEMU spacesuits, pilot a lunar rover, clean dust-covered solar arrays, transport supply crates, and analyze geological samples under realistic lunar gravity and dynamic solar day-night cycles.

The project addresses the challenge of simulating complex extraterrestrial operations in an accessible format by combining authentic environmental mechanics—such as regolith surface traction, battery drain, solid obstacle collision, and high-contrast crater illumination—with lightweight, rigged 3D models optimized to run smoothly on low-end devices.

This work is important because it demystifies the engineering and logistical realities of sustained lunar exploration, transforming technical Artemis-era mission concepts into an engaging, hands-on educational experience accessible to students and the public without specialized hardware.
details:
Our project is an interactive, browser-based 3D lunar mission simulation inspired by NASA’s Artemis program. Players experience a multi-stage spaceflight workflow—beginning inside an orbital Sci-Fi EVA Ready Room to inspect equipment and suit up, progressing through lunar landing operations, and conducting surface missions at the Orion Moon Outpost in the Lunar South Pole’s Shackleton Rim Sector.

Using real-time astronaut movement (WASD + pointer-lock camera) and a drivable lunar rover, players communicate with crew specialists, collect and deliver 5 critical supply crates across outpost modules (Command Control, Electricity, Storage Pod, Geology Lab, and Habitat Airlock), gather 6 In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) geological samples, and manage live mission telemetry including rover battery charge, water reserves ($H_2O$), power output, and dynamic lunar day-night solar cycles.
